title: Incomplete Tribes · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Incomplete Tribes is an essay on a dangerous question: must humanity become good before civilization works?

direction.delivery: Name the book plainly, then pose the question for real, lifting on 'good before'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its answer is architectural: change the design of belonging, not human nature.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: We love, build and mourn in groups, yet loyalty can turn neighbours into enemies.

direction.delivery: Warm on the first half, quieter and graver on 'enemies'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapter Nine defines an incomplete tribe: thick cooperation without total authority over members.

direction.delivery: Measured, definitional; small pause after the colon.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A chess club may govern tournament conduct, but not a member's romantic life.

direction.delivery: Lightly wry, let the example land.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Other loyalties count as safeguards, so no group becomes the sole source of truth and affection.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Exit and dissent stay open, so disagreement is not treated as betrayal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Overlapping loyalties make people harder to sort into clean enemy camps.

direction.delivery: Clear and quietly pleased with the insight.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Peace becomes an institution that lets rivals lose without being erased.

direction.delivery: Firm on 'institution', softer on 'without being erased'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapter Fifteen tests it against AI that could become the sole interpreter of a member's world.

direction.delivery: Slightly faster and more urgent, then ease at the end.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Start with the Prelude, The Question Beneath the Question, and find hope without an ideal human.

direction.delivery: Warm and direct; speak the chapter title as a title.
